Instant appeal filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short "the Act"), lays
challenge to award dated 9.6.2017, passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-(II),
Solan, District Solan, camp at Nalagarh, (in short "the Tribunal") in Claim Petition No.27-NL/2 of
2011, titled Smt. Balbinder Kaur and Ors. v. Darshan Singh and Ors, whereby the Tribunal below
while allowing claim petition having been filed by the respondents-claimants (hereinafter referred
to as "the claimants") .
under Section 166 of the Act, saddled the appellant-Insurance Company with liability to pay
compensation to the tune of Rs. 14,07,800/- to the claimants alongwith interest @8% p.a. from the
date of filing of the petition till realization.
2. Briefly stated facts, as emerge from the record, are that on 5.6.2010 at around 12:00Pm, truck

registration No. Mp-09Hf-
5552, met with an accident near Refinery Road Bridge, Panipat, Haryana on National Highway, as a
result of which, person namely Surender Singh, who at that relevant time, was travelling in the truck
in question as cleaner suffered multiple injuries and ultimately passed away while being taken to
Pgi Chandgarh for treatment.

Claimants No. 1 to 4 being widow, children and mother of the
aforesaid deceased Surender Singh, filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking therein compensation on account of death of aforesaid deceased Surender Singh on the
ground that they were fully dependent upon the deceased, who while rendering his service as
cleaner was getting salary of Rs. 5,000/- per month.

Claimants also claimed that apart from
aforesaid salary, deceased used to earn Rs.
100/- as daily allowance and was also earning Rs. 3,000/- per month from the agricultural pursuit.

3. Aforesaid claim put forth by the claimants came to be resisted .
by respondents No. 5 and 6 (owner and driver of the vehicle in question),

wherein they though
admitted factum with regard to accident, but denied that accident occurred on account of rash and
negligent driving of respondent No.6 Paramjit Singh.

Afore respondents while claiming that
respondent No.6 was having valid and effective licence at the time of the accident claimed that since
offending vehicle was insured with the appellant-insurance company, compensation, if any, on
account of death of Surender Singh is to be given by the appellant-insurance company being insurer.
4. Appellant-insurance company refuted the claim of the claimants on the ground that offending
vehicle was being plied in contravention of the terms and conditions of the policy issued by
_____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
2

appellant-insurance company and at the time of the accident, respondent No.6 was not possessing
valid and effective driving licence.

5. On the basis of aforesaid pleadings adduced on record by the respective parties, tribunal below
framed following issues:
"1.Whether Surender Singh died in a motor accident on account of rash and negligent
driving of respondent No.1, as alleged?

Opp.
2.

If issue No.1 is proved in affirmative, whether the petitioners are entitled for
compensation if so, to what amount and from whom?

Opp.
3.

Whether the petition is not maintainable in the present form? Opr-3.
4.

Whether the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and .
effective driving licence on the date of accident as alleged? Opr-3.
5.Whether the vehicle was being driven by respondent No.2 in the breach of terms of
the insurance policy as alleged? Opr-3
6. Relief."
6.

Subsequently, vide impugned award dated 9.6.2017, tribunal below held the claimants entitled for
compensation to the tune of Rs.
14,07,800/-, but since liability to pay aforesaid amount came to be fastened upon the
appellant-insurance company, it has approached this Court in the instant appeal, praying therein to
set-aside the aforesaid impugned award in as much as liabilit
y has been fastened upon the appellant-insurance company.
7. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone through records of the case.
8. Primarily, challenge to the award in the instant proceedings has been laid on the ground that tribunal below failed to afford proper opportunity to the appellant to lead the evidence.

Mr. Jagdish Thakur, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company, argued that though appellant had taken steps for summoning the Civil Ahlmad of learned JMIC at Panipat, Haryana and Sub-Inspector Parkash Chand, but yet court below failed to secure their presence by passing appropriate orders.

He further submitted that prayer made on behalf of the witnesses to record his statement through Video Conference was also not accepted by .
the court below.
While making this Court peruse FIR Ext.P2, Mr. Thakur vehemently argued that deceased Surender was not a cleaner, but at the relevant time, he was driving the offending vehicle.

He argued that since aforesaid deceased Surender was not having valid licence, claimants in _____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
3 connivance with the owner of the offending vehicle lodged false claim claiming therein deceased Surender to be cleaner.

Mr. Thakur further submitted that since deceased Surender was not having valid licence, there was no occasion r for the appellant-insurance company to award compensation in lieu of his death, but at best, court below having taken note of the fact that premium was taken by the appellant-insurance company, qua driver while issuing insurance cover, it would have awarded compensation, if any, under the workman Compensation Act.

Mr. Thakur further argued that bare perusal of the evidence led on record, especially photographs of accidental truck placed on record in the police challan filed in the FIR detailed herein above, clearly reveal that driver side of the vehicle was badly crushed and there was no possibility of driver to have survived or getting unhurt.
However, in the instant case, driver Paramjit respondent No.6 has been shown to have suffered injury on his foot, which is highly improbable.

He further submitted that though deceased Surender was not engaged as cleaner, but even otherwise, tribunal below has fallen in grave .
error while taking his income as Rs.6,000/- per month, because in the year, 2011, minimum wages under Minimum Wages Act payable to the cleaner was Rs. 3600/- per month and as such, impugned award needs to be modified accordingly.

While referring to the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi and Ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680, Mr. Thakur argued that court below has erred in giving 30% of addition in the income of the deceased because as per aforesaid judgment, only addition of 25% could be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi and Ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also argued that tribunal below has further erred in awarding Rs.1.00 lac, on account of loss of consortium, loss of love and affection.

He argued that as per Pranay Sethi judgment(supra), only sum of Rs. 15,000/- could have been awarded on account of funeral expenses, whereas in the case at hand, Tribunal below proceeded to award Rs.25,000/-.
Lastly Mr. Thakur argued that interest awarded to the claimants @ 8 % being on higher side needs to be modified.

9. Mr. Ashok Kumar, learned counsel for the claimants/respondents No. 1 to 4 vehemently argued that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned award and as such, no interference is called for.
10.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused .
material available on record, this Court finds that though perusal of FIR Ext.P2 reveals that complainant Vikas had got recorded in his statement that offending vehicle at the time of the accident was being driven by Surender Kumar, not Paramjit Singh respondent No.6, but charge sheet filed in the aforesaid FIR Ex.RX-1 duly proved by respondent No.6 clearly indicates that subsequently, during investigation, it was found that offending vehicle was being driven by respondent No.6 rashly and negligently.
It is not in dispute that in the aforesaid FIR, respondent No.6 was charge sheeted on account of his rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle on the date of the alleged incident.

Apart from above, this Court finds from the perusal of the copy of the statement/affidavit of Sh.
Gajan Singh, who at the time of the accident was also travelling in the offending vehicle alongwith deceased Surender and driver Paramjit PW6 that he as well as driver Paramjit had jumped, whereas deceased who was sitting on the rear seat of the ill fated vehicle suffered multiple injuries.

No doubt,
_____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
4

careful perusal of Ext.P2 i.e. copy of FIR suggests that complainant Vikas had categorically stated to the police that vehicle was being driven by the deceased Surender, but since aforesaid person namely Vikas never came to be examined, coupled with the fact that subsequently, during investigation police found that vehicle was being driven by Paramjit .

respondent No.6, no illegality or infirmity can be said to have been committed by the court below while returning finding that at the time of the accident, vehicle was being driven by respondent No.6 Paramjit Singh, not by the deceased Surinder.

11. Careful perusal of zimini orders passed by the learned tribunal below clearly reveal that bailable warrants were issued against the Sub Inspector Parkash Chand, but same were received back unexecuted.
Notice under Order 16 Rule 12 CPC was also issued against the aforesaid witness.
Zimini order dated 7.9.2016, suggests that summons were also issued to Civil Ahlmad to the court of JMIC Panipat.

Having perused zimini orders passed by the court below, this Court finds that despite there being bailable warrants issued by the court to secure the presence of Civil Ahlmad of JMIC and Sub-inspector Parkash Chand, aforesaid persons failed to put in appearance and as such, vide order dated 6.4.2017, court below summoned RW Incharge GRR Panipat for 8.5.2017 on filing of PF to record the statement of the witness through video conferencing, however, on 8.5.2017, learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company tendered in evidence copy of FIR Ex.Rx-1,
photographs Ex.RX-3 to Ex.Rx-7, release order Ext.Rx-8 and closed the evidence.

12. Having perused record especially zimini orders passed by the .
tribunal below, this court finds no force in the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company that court below failed to afford due opportunity to the appellant-insurance company to examine the witnesses.
To the contrary, despite repeated opportunities, appellant- insurance Company failed to lead any oral evidence as well as documentary evidence as detailed herein above.

Most importantly, appellant-insurance Company failed to examine Sh. Paramjit Singh (respondent No.6) to prove that on the date of alleged incident, vehicle was not being driven by him,
rather by deceased Surender.

There is nothing on record suggestive of the fact that steps, if any,
were taken by the appellant-insurance company to summon person namely Vikas, at whose instance, FIR came to be lodged.

Leaving everything aside, once it stood recorded in the final report filed under Section 173 filed in the FIR that vehicle on the date of the alleged incident was being driven by respondent No.6 Paramjit Aingh, no advantage, if any, can be taken by the Appellant-Insurance Company from the fact, if any recorded in the FIR with regard to driving of the vehicle by the deceased Surender.

13. Though Mr. Jagdish Thakur, attempted to argue that the liability to pay compensation, if any, by the appellant-insurance company was under workman compensation Act, but since such plea never _____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
5 came to .
be raised in the proceedings before the court below, appellant-insurance company cannot be permitted to raise such plea at this stage, especially when it stands established on record that at the time of the alleged incident, vehicle was being driven by Paramjit Singh respondent No.6 and deceased Surender Singh was employed as cleaner.

Hence, no illegality can be said to have been committed by the court below while returning finding qua issue No.1 that "whether deceased Surender Singh died in the accident on account of rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.6 Paramjit Singh.?"

However, this Court finds force in the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company that tribunal below erred in awarding sum of Rs. 1.00 lac in favour of the respondents claimants on account of loss of consortium and loss of estate, loss of love and affection to wife of the deceased.

14. The Hon'ble Apex Court in its judgment rendered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi and Ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 has held that no amount, if any, can be awarded under the head of loss of love and affection and as such, award made in this regard by the learned Tribunal below needs to be modified.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Pranay Sethi and Ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Para 59 of Pranay Sethi's judgment reads as under:-
"59.
In view of the aforesaid analysis, we proceed to record our .
conclusions:-

59.1. The two-Judge Bench in Santosh Devi should have been well advised to refer the matter to a larger Bench as it was taking a different view than what has been stated in Sarla Verma, a judgment by a coordinate Bench.
It is because a coordinate Bench of the same strength cannot take a contrary view than what has been held by another coordinate Bench.
59.2 As Rajesh has not taken note of the decision in Reshma Kumari, which was delivered at earlier point of time, the decision in Rajesh is not a binding precedent.

59.3 While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
59.4 In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for .
personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.
59.6 The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
59.7 The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.

59.8 Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.
15,000/, Rs. 40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years."
15. As per the aforesaid judgment, only sum of Rs. 40,000/- on account of loss of consortium can be awarded to the wife.

16. Similarly, this court finds that on account of funeral expenses and loss of estate, only sum of Rs.
15,000/- could be awarded, whereas in the instant case, Tribunal below has awarded sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- on account of loss of consortium and loss of estate and sum of Rs. 25000/- on account of funeral expenses.

17. While placing reliance upon latest judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V. Smt. Somwati and Ors, in Civil appeal No. 3093 of 2020 (a/w connected matters), Mr. Dinesh Bhanot, learned counsel representing the .
claimants submitted that sum of Rs. 40,000/- each, is also required to be awarded in favour of claimants No. 1 and 2 being filial consortium.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V. Smt. Somwati and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Otherwise also, Hon'ble Apex Court in its judgment rendered in case titled Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and Ors, (2018) 18 SCC 130, which has been also taken note of, in Somwati's case, has laid down that consortium is not limited to spousal consortium and it also includes parental consortium as well as filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and Ors, (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having taken note of the aforesaid judgment rendered by Three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance's case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court in its latest judgment passed in Somwati's case (supra) has held as under :-
"35.

The Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi has also not under conventional head included any compensation towards 'loss of love and affection' which have been now further reiterated by three- Judge Bench in United India Insurance Company Ltd.
(supra).

It is thus now authoritatively well settled that no compensation can be _____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
7 awarded under the head 'loss of love and affection'.
36. The word 'consortium' has been defined in Black's law Dictionary, 10th edition.

The Black's law dictionary also simultaneously notices the filial consortium, parental consortium and spousal consortium in following manner:-
"Consortium 1. The benefits that one person, esp. A spouse, is entitled to receive from another, including companionship, cooperation, affection, aid, financial support, and (between spouses) sexual relations a claim for loss of consortium.
 Filial consortium

A child's society, affection, and .
companionship given to a parent.
Parental consortium
A parent's society, affection and companionship given to a child.
Spousal consortium
A spouse's society, affection and companionship given to the other spouse."

37. The Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. (Supra) as well as United India Insurance Company ltd.(Supra), Three-Judge Bench laid down that the consortium is not limited to spousal consortium and it also includes parental consortium as well as filial consortium.
In paragraph 87 of United India Insurance Company Ltd. (supra), 'consortium' to all the three claimants was thus awarded.

Paragraph 87 is quoted below:-
"87.
Insofar as the conventional heads are concerned, the deceased Satpal Singh left behind a widow and three children r as his dependants.

On the basis of the judgments in Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma General (supra), the following amounts are awarded under the conventional heads:-
i) Loss of Estate: Rs. 15,000 ii) Loss of Consortium:
a) Spousal Consortium: Rs.40,000 b) Parental Consortium: 40,000 x 3 = Rs.
1,20,000 iii) Funeral Expenses: Rs. 15,000"
_____________________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Balbinder Kaur And Ors on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91454882/
8 38.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that Pranay Sethi has only referred to spousal consortium and no other consortium was referred to in the judgment of Pranay Sethi, hence, there is no justification for allowing the parental consortium and filial consortium.

The Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi has referred to amount of Rs.40,000/- to the 'loss of consortium' but the Constitution Bench had not addressed the issue as to whether consortium of Rs.40,000/- is only payable as spousal consortium.
The judgment of Pranay Sethi cannot be read to mean that it lays down the proposition that the consortium is payable only to the wife.
39. The Three-Judge Bench in United India Insurance Company Ltd. (Supra) has categorically laid down that apart from spousal consortium, parental and filial consortium is payable.
We feel ourselves bound by the above judgment of Three Judge Bench.
We, thus, cannot accept the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant that the amount of consortium awarded to each of the claimants is not sustainable.

40. We, thus, found the impugned judgments of the High Court .
awarding consortium to each of the claimants in accordance with law which does not warrant any interference in this appeal.
We, however, accept the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant that there is no justification for award of compensation under separate head 'loss of love and affection'.

The appeal filed by the appellant deserves to be allowed insofar as the award of compensation under the head 'loss of love and affection."
18.

Similarly, this court finds that on account of funeral charges, sum of Rs. 15,000/- could be awarded and on account of future prospects,
19.
r to 25% addition is to be made.
This Court finds that interest awarded by the court below @ 8% is on higher side and as such, same needs to be modified

This Court finds from the record that no cogent and convincing evidence ever came to be led on record on behalf of the claimants that he was earning Rs. 6000/- per month and as such, tribunal below ought to have calculated the income of the deceased on the basis of Minimum Wages Act, who at the relevant time was working as cleaner.

Since it stands established on record that deceased Surender was working as cleaner at the time of the accident and claimants were unable to place on record salary certificate, court below ought to have calculated monthly income of the deceased by taking into consideration minimum wages payable to cleaner i.e. semi skilled, in the year 2011, which as per notification made available to this court was Rs.120 per day, meaning thereby, monthly income at the time of the accident of the deceased was Rs. 3600/-.
As per judgment supra, an addition of 25% could have been made in the instant .
case and as such, income of the deceased needs to be modified accordingly.

21. In view of the discussions made supra and the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the afore-cited judgments, this Court deems it fit to modify the award passed by learned Tribunal below as under:

22. Rate of interest awarded on the amount of compensation being on higher side is also required to be reduced to 6%.
Ordered accordingly.

23. Consequently, in view of detailed discussion made herein above and law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, present appeal is partly allowed and impugned award passed by learned Tribunal below is modified to aforesaid extent only.

Accordingly, present appeal is disposed of,
alongwith all pending applications, if any.
Interim directions, if any, are vacated.
